title: Understanding Social Capital and Community Bonds
text:
Social capital refers to the resources derived from social networks and relationships, acting as a form of collective wealth within a community. These ties—whether strong (close family) or weak (colleagues)—can facilitate access to information, opportunities, and support necessary for individual advancement and group stability.

Researchers distinguish between different types of capital, notably bonding social capital which connects homogeneous groups, and bridging social capital which links diverse, disparate networks. While both are valuable, excessive reliance on one type can limit a community's overall resilience and adaptability in the face of systemic change.

The concept suggests that societal function is not purely predicated on physical infrastructure or economic wealth alone, but significantly depends upon the quality and density of interpersonal trust and mutual obligation shared among its members.
